cards.text: Jesus has just said that the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. The people are still listening, and Jesus is getting close to Jerusalem. So He tells them a parable, and friend, He's telling this one for a reason.

cards.question: Jesus is near Jerusalem when He tells this parable. What were the people thinking that made Him tell it?

answers.text: God's kingdom would appear any moment
Only priests could enter God's kingdom

cards.text: So Jesus starts the story: a man of noble birth heads to a distant country to lay claim to his kingship and then return. Before he goes, he hands ten of his servants ten minas, one each.

cards.question: Before he leaves, the man tells his servants to keep the money tucked away safely until he returns.

cards.text: But his subjects hated him, and they send a delegation after him with a message. Friend, that's not a complaint. That's a ROAD TRIP of complaining.

cards.question: What message does the subjects' delegation carry after the man?

answers.text: They don't want him ruling over them
They want him to hurry back home
They want his servants in charge

cards.question: When the man comes back with his kingship, he calls in the servants he gave the money to, so he can find out what each one earned.

cards.text: The first servant steps up, and his one mina has produced TEN more minas. Friend, I once turned one bag of chocolate chips into zero bags, and I never even left the counter.

cards.question: The master says, Well done, and praises the first servant for being ___ in a very small matter.
What reward does the master give the first servant?

answers.text: A seat at the king's table

cards.question: The second servant's mina has made five minas. The master gives him authority over five ___.

cards.text: Then another servant comes in: "Master, here is your mina, which I have laid away in a piece of cloth." That mina sat wrapped up in the dark the whole time, and friend, after my years in the back of a junk drawer, I KNOW how it feels.

cards.question: This servant says he put the mina away because he was afraid of the master.

cards.text: He even tells the master to his face that he's a harsh man, which is a BOLD thing to say to the guy who decides what happens to you next. The master answers, "You wicked servant, I will judge you by your own words."

cards.question: The master says that if this servant thought he was harsh, there was one simple thing he could have done with the mina. What is it?

answers.text: Put it in the bank to earn interest
Handed it to a neighbor to keep
Traded it for a small piece of land

cards.text: Then the master gives an order to those standing by: take the mina away from him.

cards.question: The master says to give that mina to the servant who has ___ minas.

cards.text: The people standing by speak up: "Master," they said, "he already has ten!" It's like watching the coworker who just got a raise ALSO win the office raffle.

cards.question: The master answers that everyone who has will be given more, and the one who does not have will be given a fresh start.
One group from the start of the story still hasn't been dealt with. Who does the master turn to last?

answers.text: The enemies who didn't want him as king
The servants who stood by watching
The second servant with five minas

cards.text: His order for them is a heavy one: bring those enemies who were unwilling for him to rule over them, and slay them in front of him. And that's where Jesus ends the parable.

findings.problem: Story card 5 says the subjects 'hated him' and jokes about a 'road trip of complaining.' That rules out the wrong answer 'They want him to hurry back home' and weakens 'They want his servants in charge,' so only the right answer is left standing.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The joke turns 'one bag of chocolate chips into zero bags' while he 'never even left the counter.' It is the reverse of the servant's action, not the same action. The punchline also leaves a stranger asking 'huh?': did he eat them, lose them, or something else?

rule.text: The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to fill in the master's exact word ('faithful') in a line they haven't seen. 'Clever' is just as reasonable for a servant who turned one mina into ten, so the baker is guessing the wording rather than reasoning about meaning.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card cites Luke 19:18-19, but its right answer ('cities') comes only from Luke 19:19.

rule.text: A choice card cites only the verses of its right answer.

findings.problem: The third servant's reason for calling the master harsh is never told on any card: 'You withdraw what you did not deposit and reap what you did not sow' (Luke 19:21). The master's reply in Luke 19:22 turns those same words back on him. The card cites Luke 19:21-22 but leaves out the detail the master's judgment rests on.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The question asks who the master 'turns to last.' In Luke 19:26-27 he is still speaking to those standing by and gives his order about the enemies to them. A baker could argue that 'The servants who stood by watching' is right, because those are the people he addresses.

rule.text: A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.
